newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends lower on commission house sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends lower on commission house sales.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower Thursday, with soymeal under pressure from commission house selling and falling basis levels, floor traders said.
Rosenthal was a prominent seller in soymeal futures, selling 500 lots in late trade, floor sources said.
Both the soyoil and soymeal trading saw very light volume on the day following the Christmas holiday, which helped to amplify losses in both pits, floor sources said.
CBOT soymeal futures were also under pressure from a drop in basis values for soymeal in cash markets this week, cash and futures sources said.
Crushers have made only modest cutbacks in soymeal production over the holiday, while demand from domestic end-users is being satisfied by pre-Christmas purchases, traders said.
Soyoil values were underpinned by news that China bought 26,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for January shipment on Tuesday, trader said.
January soymeal ended down $2.00 per ton at $230.90, and March soymeal $2.90 at $221.20 per ton. January soyoil ended down 0.16 cent per pound at 22.88, and March ended down 0.11 cent at 23.30.
One source said that firms with ties to the cash soymeal market were covering short futures positions, which helped to limit gains.
On the day, Chicago Corp bought 250 lots March soyoil and Tradelink bought 200 March. ADM sold 100 lots March soyoil and Merrill Lynch sold 150 lots January.
In soymeal trade for the session, Refco sold 150 lots January and Cargill sold 100 January and 100 March. Produce Grain bought 100 January and E.D. & F. Man bought 150 January.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, higher than Tuesday's volume of 10,427 contracts.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, up from the 8,447 contracts reported Tuesday.
